content.title: About
content.content: Sweet potato fries are thin strips of sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) that are cooked until crisp. Sweet potatoes are cultivated in warm climates, have a naturally sweet flavor, bright orange flesh, and are rich in beta‑carotene.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potatoes belong to the morning‑glory family, not to the true potato family.
They contain two‑to‑three times more vitamin A than regular potatoes.
Sweet potatoes were domesticated in South America over 5,000 years ago.
Proper frying retains most of the fiber and antioxidants.
In many countries sweet potato fries are a staple in school cafeterias.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Good source of potassium
items.content: Potassium supports heart function, muscle contraction, and fluid balance.

items.title: Lower glycemic impact when baked
items.content: Baking or air‑frying sweet potatoes results in a lower glycemic index compared with regular potatoes.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Anthocyanins and vitamin C protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High carbohydrate content
items.content: Large portions can raise blood glucose, which is important for people with diabetes.

items.title: Oil frying
items.content: Deep‑frying in excess oil adds calories and may introduce trans fats if the wrong oil is used.

items.title: Nightshade allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to sweet potatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve sweet potato fries hot, seasoned with salt, spices, or herbs. They can be baked, air‑fried, or deep‑fried and pair well with yogurt‑based dips, guacamole, or classic ketchup.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked fries keep in the refrigerator in an airtight container for 2‑3 days. Raw sweet potato sticks should be stored in a cool, dry place, and for longer storage kept refrigerated wrapped in plastic.
